extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and parties appearing before the PTAB (petitioners, patent owners, counsel for IPR/PGR/derivation proceedings)
extracted.subtask_description: Practice and procedural guidance for conducting AIA trial proceedings before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (inter partes review, post-grant review, derivation proceedings), covering jurisdiction, filing requirements, discovery, motions, hearings, and final decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. § 6(b) provides that the Board is to conduct derivation proceedings, inter partes reviews, and post‑grant reviews; the Board will have exclusive jurisdiction within the Office over every application and patent involved in those proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ex parte reexamination and inter partes reexamination proceedings are not 'involved' patents for derivation, IPR, and PGR and are treated separately except as ordered by the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on ex parte communications
rubrics_metrics.description: All substantive communications with the Board regarding a proceeding must include all parties to the proceeding, except as otherwise authorized. 37 C.F.R. § 42.5(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted exceptions include ministerial communications with staff, conference calls/hearings where opposing counsel declines to participate, informing the Board of status of related Board proceedings, and citing a pending case for a general proposition. Parties should meet and confer before requesting Board calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arranging a conference call with the Board
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may request conference calls to raise and resolve issues in an expedited manner after meeting and conferring; parties should be prepared to explain why the call is needed and what materials may be needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify if a court reporter will be present; transcript must be filed as an exhibit within one week of receipt. Board expects many procedural issues to be handled during conference calls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal to participate in conference/hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may permit a hearing or conference call to take place even if a party refuses to participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board may impose safeguards (e.g., recording and entry of the recording into the record) as conditions for holding the call/hearing when a party refuses to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for lead and back-up counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: A party represented by counsel must designate both a lead and a back-up counsel who can conduct business on behalf of the lead counsel. 37 C.F.R. § 42.10(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead counsel is expected to participate in hearings and sign papers; back-up counsel conducts business when lead is unavailable and may participate in hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of attorney filing
rubrics_metrics.description: A power of attorney must be filed with the designation of counsel, unless the designated counsel is already counsel of record. 37 C.F.R. § 42.10(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure proper power of attorney to avoid procedural problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro hac vice admission
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may recognize counsel pro hac vice upon a showing of good cause, subject to the requirement that lead counsel is a registered practitioner. 37 C.F.R. § 42.10(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant or revocation is discretionary and may consider complexity, competence, adherence to Office Rules of Professional Conduct, and civility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing as default
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic filing is the default manner for filing documents with the Board. 37 C.F.R. § 42.6(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper filing requires a motion explaining the need; parties may request one‑day extensions for demonstrated electronic filing problems during business hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must provide mandatory notices including identification of real parties‑in‑interest, related matters, lead and back‑up counsel, and service information. 37 C.F.R. § 42.8; revised notices must be filed within 21 days of change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These notices assist Board in identifying conflicts and applying statutory estoppel provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real party‑in‑interest and privy identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must identify real parties‑in‑interest or privies to assist the Board in identifying conflicts and to ensure proper application of statutory estoppel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The determination is fact‑dependent; Board applies flexible common‑law principles (control, relationship to petition, funding/directing of petition). No bright‑line test; evaluate control, relationship to petition, and nature of the filing entity on a case‑by‑case basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of related matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must identify any other judicial or administrative matter that would affect or be affected by a decision in the proceeding, including federal court cases and related patent/application matters and reexaminations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps Board coordinate proceedings, decide stays, consolidation, or termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service information identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties are required to provide service information to allow efficient communication between the Board and the parties. 37 C.F.R. § 42.8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service may be made electronically by agreement; maintaining a proper correspondence address is responsibility of applicant/patent owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of the record
rubrics_metrics.description: The record of a proceeding, including documents and things, shall be made available to the public except as otherwise ordered. 37 C.F.R. § 42.14.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents remain public unless a motion to seal is filed and granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential information and protective orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential information is identified consistent with FRCP 26(c)(1)(G); protective orders may be issued for good cause to protect trade secrets or confidential research, development, or commercial information. 37 C.F.R. § 42.54.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protective orders must be proposed by parties and approved by the Board; guidelines and a default protective order are in Appendix B.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to seal procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion to seal may be filed concurrent with the document; the document will be provisionally sealed pending decision on the motion. 37 C.F.R. § 42.14.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing confidential information with a petition, a petitioner may file a motion to seal and need not serve the sealed confidential information. Patent owner access prior to institution depends on agreement to protective order or entry of one by the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expungement of confidential information
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential information subject to a protective order ordinarily becomes public 45 days after denial of a petition to institute or 45 days after final judgment in a trial; a party may file a motion to expunge before that time. 37 C.F.R. § 42.56.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board encourages redacting sensitive information where possible rather than sealing entire documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sealing/conception dates in derivation
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties in derivation proceedings may file conception dates under seal and may request that an opponent not be given access until the opponent’s conception dates have been provided to the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This balances protecting sensitive inventorship information with need for fair adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequenced discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery proceeds in a sequenced fashion after institution to streamline proceedings and narrow scope; patent owner discovery typically precedes petitioner discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequencing allows meaningful discovery before motions and oppositions, with Board setting times in Scheduling Order; scope focused on what parties reasonably need to respond to grounds raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine discovery scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Routine discovery includes production of any exhibit cited in a paper or testimony, cross‑examination of opponent's declarants, and relevant information inconsistent with a party's positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board authorization not required for routine discovery but Scheduling Order will set times; routine discovery places parties on a level playing field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inconsistent statements disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must disclose non‑privileged materials inconsistent with contentions in affidavits/declarations (examples provided where petitioner's own work contradicts expert affidavit or patent owner must disclose non‑privileged evidence rebutting asserted surprising results).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate when disclosures of inconsistent statements are required to ensure fair record and credibility assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Witness expenses and document translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery provisions address witness expenses and the need to translate documents as appropriate to ensure meaningful use of evidence in proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board may provide further directions in Scheduling Order; parties should plan for translation costs and witness logistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compelled testimony and additional discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures exist for compelled testimony and additional discovery beyond routine discovery when necessary to develop a fair record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such discovery is handled by Board order; parties should justify additional discovery as focused on issues raised by the opponent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory initial disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules include requirements for mandatory initial disclosures to aid development of the record and assessment of credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details and timing are set forth in the rules and the Scheduling Order to streamline discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live testimony in trial
rubrics_metrics.description: Live testimony may be permitted at the oral hearing where the panel believes it will help making a determination, particularly where witness demeanor is critical to credibility (e.g., antedating by reduction to practice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests are considered case‑by‑case; live testimony becomes part of the record and must not exceed the scope of the underlying declaration; panel may direct questions to witnesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: E‑discovery model and guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Model Order Regarding E‑Discovery (Appendix C) provides guidance for handling electronic discovery in PTAB trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should follow Appendix C and meet and confer on e‑discovery issues; Board may adopt the model order or tailor e‑discovery per case needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: Expert testimony is a recognized part of the evidentiary record and subject to usual admissibility considerations and the Federal Rules of Evidence as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expert declarations should disclose underlying facts/data; routine discovery and depositions of expert declarants are part of procedures to test credibility and sufficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: General motions practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions practice is governed by the trial rules; some motions require prior authorization and the Scheduling Order will set word counts and page limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board provides guidance on timing, prior authorization, and expects parties to follow word limits; motions to strike, exclude, or for joinder have particular considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word count and page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board uses word counts and page limits for briefs and motions consistent with the rules and Scheduling Orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should follow the Board's word count rules and request leave when exceeding limits; word counts affect efficiency and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testimony must disclose underlying facts or data
rubrics_metrics.description: Testimony (e.g., expert affidavits) must disclose the underlying facts or data relied upon to support assertions in the declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declarations lacking disclosure of underlying data may be subject to discovery orders, motions to exclude, or may be given less weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of tests and data and objective indicia of nonobviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties relying on tests, experimental data, or secondary considerations (objective indicia) must provide supporting evidence and explanation to substantiate assertions regarding nonobviousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner relying on surprising/unexpected results should provide non‑privileged evidence and may be required to disclose inconsistent materials; Board may analyze strengths/weaknesses of such evidence at institution and trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition filing minimum procedural compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition must be filed consistent with statutory time periods and accompanied by the evidence the petitioner seeks to rely upon (see 35 U.S.C. §§ 135(a), 311(c); 37 C.F.R. § 42.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing date and minimum procedural compliance are critical; failure can affect institution and filing date determinations (see examples and precedents referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof for statutory institution thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director or Board may institute a trial where the petitioner establishes that the standards for instituting the requested trial are met, taking into account any preliminary response; conversely, the Board may deny institution if the petition fails to meet standards. See 35 U.S.C. §§ 314, 324.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For IPR/PGR, institution is an evaluative decision within statutory framework; Board will analyze whether petition shows reasonable likelihood or likelihood under applicable standard and will provide analyses to guide trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific requirements for petitions (claim charts and claim construction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions must identify all claims challenged and the grounds and supporting evidence on a claim‑by‑claim basis; may include claim charts and claim construction positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition should present grounds clearly and thoroughly; claim construction positions and properly prepared claim charts support the Board’s assessment at institution and guide trial scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner preliminary response
rubrics_metrics.description: In IPR and PGR, patent owner may file a preliminary response within three months of notification of a filing date and may elect not to respond. See 35 U.S.C. §§ 313, 323.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary response may affect institution decision; Board considers petition taking into account any preliminary response when deciding whether to institute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory threshold standards for institution (IPR/PGR/Derivation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different statutory thresholds exist for institution depending on proceeding (e.g., IPR and PGR have statutory standards in §§ 314, 324; derivation has its own standards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board will apply the applicable statutory standard when deciding institution and may deny, institute on all claims, or institute on none (post‑SAS Institute v. Iancu the Board will not institute on fewer than all claims or challenges in a petition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations in instituting a review (including parallel petitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board considers statutory thresholds, preliminary responses, related matters, and may consider issues like parallel petitions and 35 U.S.C. § 325(d) (duplicative petitions) when deciding institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When multiple matters involve the same patent, the Board may stay, transfer, consolidate, or terminate matters; Board will consider how to handle parallel petitions challenging the same patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of decisions on whether to institute
rubrics_metrics.description: When instituting a trial, the Board generally will provide analysis of strengths and weaknesses of all challenges in the petition to provide guidance to parties for trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A party dissatisfied with the decision to institute may request rehearing for matters believed overlooked or misapprehended (37 C.F.R. §§ 42.71(c), (d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling Order and trial timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board will enter a Scheduling Order when a trial is instituted setting due dates for trial and sequencing to ensure completion within one year of institution (subject to statutory extensions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample scheduling orders provided in Appendix A; orders set deadlines for discovery, patent owner response, motions to amend, petitioner replies, sur‑replies, and timing for oral hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial conference call (one month after institution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may request an initial conference call about one month after institution to discuss intended motions and whether Scheduling Order adjustment is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board uses the call to discuss scheduling, motions, and may handle procedural issues quickly; parties should meet and confer beforehand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions to amend practice and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions to amend are available in IPR and PGR subject to rules: content requirements, due dates, evidentiary standards, and claim construction considerations; Board evaluates amendments under applicable statutory and rule standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix and guidance (including pilot programs) describe practice; motions to amend should disclose support for proposed substitute claims, show patentability, and follow timing constraints; opposition and reply practice is specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to a motion to amend
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner may oppose a patent owner's motion to amend; opposition practice and timing are set in the Scheduling Order and rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposition should address patentability of proposed claims and any procedural defects; parties may file motions to exclude evidence submitted with motions to amend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replies, sur‑replies, and scope of permissible briefing
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may file replies to patent owner responses and oppositions to motions to amend, and sur‑replies as allowed; scope of replies/sur‑replies is limited to matters within the proper scope of the underlying brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board discourages new issues in replies; new arguments or evidence may be struck or disregarded; authorization to file sur‑replies is discretionary and guided by Scheduling Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions for joinder
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may file motions for joinder to join other parties in a proceeding; joinder practice is governed by the rules and Board discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joinder may affect scheduling and institution deadlines; Board considers statutory limits and fairness in granting joinder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenging admissibility; motions to exclude and strike
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may move to exclude evidence believed inadmissible or to strike new issues/evidence; motions to strike are exceptional remedies and will be granted rarely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motions to strike should generally be requested within one week of the allegedly improper submission; Board prefers resolving scope/weight issues rather than striking unless prejudice warrants it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party will be afforded an opportunity to present their case before at least three Board members; timing, pre‑hearing conference, and format will be set in the Scheduling Order (typically about one hour per side unless adjusted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre‑hearing conference held ≤15 days before hearing to identify issues panel wants addressed; petitioner generally argues first, then patent owner, then petitioner rebuttal; parties should confer on time and format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrative exhibits at hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrative exhibits are aids to oral argument, not evidence, and should be simple (slides and handouts); pages should be numbered and marked 'DEMONSTRATIVE EXHIBIT – NOT EVIDENCE'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elaborate demonstratives may impede argument; demonstratives cannot introduce new evidence or arguments; parties should exchange and resolve demonstratives ahead of filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live testimony at oral hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Live testimony is permitted when panel finds it helpful (e.g., demeanor critical to credibility); format is left to panel discretion, and testimony must not exceed scope of the underlying declaration or present new theories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for live testimony should explain why demeanor or issue is critical and may be granted more frequently when testimony is case‑dispositive.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new evidence or arguments at oral hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may only present arguments relied on in previously submitted papers and evidence previously submitted in the proceeding; except when Board permits live testimony, no new evidence is allowed at oral hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New theories raised at oral argument may be disregarded; Board may limit live testimony to scope of prior declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special equipment and accessibility at hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Hearing rooms have projectors for PowerPoint; parties should advise Board of special needs (wheelchair space, easel, overhead projector) in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume availability of equipment; notify Board Trial Division paralegal early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement preference and practice
rubrics_metrics.description: There are strong public policy reasons to favor settlement; parties may file settlement agreements to terminate proceedings unless Board has decided merits. 35 U.S.C. §§ 317, 327.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board may facilitate or require settlement discussions and expects termination after filing a settlement agreement absent Board decision on merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final written decision timing and content
rubrics_metrics.description: For IPR and PGR, Board will enter a final written decision not more than one year from institution, extendable up to six months for good cause. 35 U.S.C. § 316(a)(11). The decision will address issues necessary to resolve the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derivation proceedings also have an expectation of a final decision within one year of institution though not statutorily required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remands from the Federal Circuit
rubrics_metrics.description: Board aims to issue decisions on remanded cases within six months of receiving the Federal Circuit mandate, with procedures varying by scope and instructions from the Federal Circuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties must contact Board within ten business days after mandate to arrange a conference call and meet and confer on proposed remand procedures; Board considers scope, need for additional briefing/evidence, and time/expense impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for rehearing
rubrics_metrics.description: A party dissatisfied with a Board decision may file a request for rehearing under 37 C.F.R. § 42.71; the burden is on the party to show the decision should be modified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request must specifically identify matters believed misapprehended or overlooked and where each matter was previously addressed; new evidence on rehearing requires showing 'good cause' to be admitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix guidance: sample scheduling orders, protective orders, e‑discovery, testimony
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendices include sample scheduling orders for IPR/PGR and derivation (A‑1, A‑2), Protective Order Guidelines including Default Protective Order (Appendix B), Model Order for E‑Discovery (Appendix C), and Testimony Guidelines (Appendix D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should consult and use appendices as templates and guidance when preparing orders and motions; Board may adopt or modify Appendix provisions per case circumstances.
